Commentary.Commentary: That is all we have for you from this series. New Zealand win the 3-match ODI series 3-0. The two teams now go on to play a 3-match Test series which begins from 28th February. Join in for that one. The first Test will be played at Seddon Park. It begins at 1100 local (2200 GMT, previous night). Until then, see you!

Victorious New Zealand captain for tonight, Tom Latham, says that the batting unit managed to get in partnerships and it was not a one-man show, which pleased him a lot. Is really happy to see Southee swinging the ball like he did. On New Zealand's improvement, Tom says that the challenge is to improve in all facets of the game. Agrees and admits that after taking a wicket, the bigger challenge is to keep taking more scalps at regular intervals.

Bangladesh captain, Mashrafe Mortaza, admits that the boys are disappointed but looks at some of the positives, mentioning Sabbir's century at the forefront. Adds that in this game, they picked up wickets regularly till the 35th over, which was the second positive. But then laments the inability to fight back after Jimmy Neesham's onslaught.

MARTIN GUPTILL HAS BEEN AWARDED THE PLAYER OF THE SERIES for his 264 runs, at an average of 132. Says that it was a nice comeback after the injury break, putting up a nice couple of performances leading to a series win. Is looking forward to play the red-ball format now and sharpen his skills. On his World Cup chances, Guppy says that one has got to be positive and believe in oneself.

TIM SOUTHEE HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH. Says that it is nice to get out in the middle and contribute to a team win and a series win. Adds that he got plenty of time to rectify some of the errors identified from the India series. Admits that there is healthy competition amongst the seamers within the unit and that is helping the team overall. Praises the batters for setting up the win which gave the bowlers some cushion to come out and take some wickets upfront. Ends by saying that every time he gets an opportunity to play for New Zealand, it is special.

Earlier in the day, New Zealand posted 330 runs on the board courtesy - fifties from Henry Nicholls, Ross Taylor and Tom Latham. Martin Guptill missed out on a rare Kiwi record of scoring three consecutive centuries. But the total proved to be more than enough with the middle order stepping up. It was another poor outing with both the bat and ball from Bangladesh. Stay tuned for the presentation.
The Kiwi bowlers started right on the money and Tim Southee started throwing venom from the very first ball. He rattled the Bangladeshi top order and he was the pick of the bowler picking up 6/65.

A very comprehensive victory for New Zealand in the end. Sabbir Rahman's lone battle went in vain. The chase started in a very disastrous manner for the visitors. They lost three wickets in three overs and were on the back foot from there and kept losing wickets. At one stage it looked like Bangladesh will struggle to go past the 100-run mark when they were 61-5. But Sabbir Rahman had decided to make the most of the life he got when he was dropped on 0. He put a 101-run stand with Mohammad Saifuddin and made sure Bangladesh bow out with some respect. His maiden century along with Saifuddin's 44 and Mehidy Hasan's 37 took Bangladesh's total to 242.

OUT! A 6-wicket haul for Tim Southee and he wraps up the Bangladesh innings. Short ball on the body. Rahman looks to pull this but gets a top edge to it. The bat comes off his hand. The ball lobs up, Southee gets under it and takes a simple catch. Sabbir has played his part but New Zealand win by 88 runs and take the series 3-0.

OUT! Top edge and taken! Brought for the kill and Boult kills it. What a spoil sport, this Latham is. Relax guys, just joking. Moving on to serious stuff, this is exactly what New Zealand wanted. He is done in by the angle of the ball as well, coming into him. He cannot bail out of the shot and miscues it. The ball limps off the top edge and Martin Guptill follows its parabolic trajectory, running back from square leg. Gets to the ball comfortably and pouches it. That ends the 101-run stand and a decent knock from Saifuddin as well. Game over? 169 more needed from 95 balls.

Good length delivery around off, Mahmudullah plays it to the fielder at point.
Bouncer. It is on leg, Mahmudullah sits under it and lets it go to Latham behind.

So close! Good length delivery on off, Mushfiqur looks to play it to the off side with a slant bat but gets an inside edge. The ball misses the stumps by just a few inches. Rahim is lucky to survive that.
Sprays this down the leg side. Rahim looks to flick it but misses. The umpire signals it as wide.
Length delivery on the stumps, Rahim keeps it away from danger.
On middle and leg, Mamudullah tucks it to the on side and takes a single.

SIX! Mahmudullah is off the mark with a maximum. Shorter in length on off and middle, Mahmudullah pulls it over mid-wicket. The boundaries are short here and the ball sails over the fence for a maximum.
Full length delivery on middle and leg, Mahmudullah defends it off his front foot.
Good length delivery pitching on leg and going away. Mahmudullah looks to flick it but gets hit on the pads.
Looks like Mushfiqur Rahim is still not comfortable and has called for pain killers.
Rahim gets behind this ball and defends this.
A short delivery which has been pulled away towards short mid-wicket.
FOUR! Edge and flies away again. Fuller ball outside off, Rahim goes after it but gets an outside edge which flies over the slip cordon and away to the third man boundary.
Outside off, goes away from Rahim who leaves it alone.

Ross Taylor has looked to have injured his finger along with Mushfiqur Rahim. The physios are on to have a look at them. It looks like it's the same finger which has been causing Mushfiqur trouble lately.

FOUR! Edge and just away. Just outside the off pole, Rahim's bottom hand comes off the bat. He gets hit on the gloves. The ball goes towards Taylor at first slip. He dives to his right but cannot get close to the ball which runs away to the third man fence.
FOUR! Just the second run off the bat after 5 overs. There was width on offer outside off, Rahim carves this over point for a boundary. After 12 balls, Rahim gets off the mark with a boundary.
Back of a length on middle and off, Mahmudullah defends it off the back foot to see off the over.
Length delivery outside off, Mahmudullah comes down the track and looks to hit it with a slant bat but misses. Not the best selection of shot, considering the match situation.

FIVE WIDES! Length delivery going down the leg side. Mahmudullah looks to flick but misses, Latham dives to his left but cannot stop it. The ball races away to the fence and the umpire signals it as wide.
Bouncer! It in on middle and leg, Mahmudullah ducks underneath it.
Back of a length delivery on middle and off, Mahmudullah blocks it away.

NOT OUT! Safe. Good length delivery pitching on leg. The ball straightens after pitching.  Mahmudullah looks to flick it but he hits his bat on his pads.  The ball hits his pad and the New Zealand players all go up in appeal. The umpire turns it down. Southee has a word with his skipper, Latham. They decide to take the review and the Hawk-Eye shows that the impact and wicket hitting were both on-field call. Hence New Zealand though retain their review.
Another one for the Kiwis? New Zealand have taken a review for an lbw decision given against him.
Wide! Bouncer gone wrong. It is on the leg side and over the head of Mahmudullah. The square leg umpire signals it as wide and the umpire gives it.
Outswinging ball which is bowled full and around off, Mahmudullah shoulders arms to it.
Gets behind this one and blocks it. Maiden from Boult.
Pace and bounce! Length outside off and 137 kph. Rahim flashes at it but fails to connect.
Pitched outside leg, Rahim misses his flick and gets hit on his thigh pad. Half-hearted appeal. Misses leg too.
Length around off, Rahim guides it to the man at point. 3 dots from the first three balls.
Another length ball close to the stumps, Rahim shoulders his arms to it.
Length ball closer to the off pole. Mushfiqur Rahim leaves it at the last movement.
On the stumps and a bit of inswing on this one. Mahmudullah blocks it to give Southee a wicket maiden. Brilliant stuff here from Tim Southee.
Good length delivery outside off, Mahmudullah shoulders arms to it.
Pitching on length, Mahmudullah defends it off his front foot.
Length delivery outside off, Mahmudullah takes no risk and lets it go to the keeper.
Good length delivery outside off, Mahmudullah leaves it alone.
Mahmudullah walks in at no. 5 in just the 3rd over.

OUT! LBW! Southee gets his third in the span of just 7 balls. Good length delivery pitching on middle and leg. The ball jags back in and Das is late to realize it. He looks to defend but gets hit on the pads. Southee thinks he has got the batsman and the umpire agrees with him and raises the finger. Das and Mushfiqur have a chat about it. They take too long and the 15-second time is over. Hawk-Eye shows that it was going to hit the leg stump. They would have lost the review had they gone upstairs. New Zealand are on fire!
Length delivery on off and middle, Rahim blocks it away. Tight start from Boult. Just one run off his first over.
Good length delivery on off, Mushfiqur plays it to the fielder at point.
Full around off, Rahim drives it to the fielder at cover.
On middle and leg, Das flicks it away towards mid-wicket for a single. He is off the mark.
Full around off, Das pushes it to the fielder at cover.
Boult starts with a good full length inswinging delivery. Liton flicks it off the inner half of the bat towards square leg.
As expected, Trent Boult will partner Tim Southee from the other end with the second new ball.
Great over by Southee. Full on off and middle, Mushfiqur Rahim does well to defend it. One run and two wickets off the first over. Perfect start for the Kiwis.
Good length delivery outside off, Rahim leaves it alone.
The new man in is Mushfiqur Rahim.

OUT! Bowled. Southee with the second wicket of the over. Length delivery on off, the ball jags back in after pitching. Sarkar gets beaten all ends up and the ball hits the middle and off stumps. Bangladesh in all kinds of trouble in the very first over.
Good length delivery on the stumps, Sarkar blocks it away.
Wide. Full and hint of away swing. It pitches on leg and goes away, Soumya looks to flick but he misses. The umpire signals it as wide.
Soumya Sarkar walks out at number 3.

OUT! Southee strikes in the very second delivery. Length delivery outside off, Tamim Iqbal recklessly comes out and tries to hit it over mid off. He gets a thick outside edge and the ball goes straight to Tom Latham behind the stumps who makes no mistake.
Southee starts with a full length delivery outside off, Tamim pushes it to the fielder at point.
We are back for the chase. Tamim Iqbal and Liton Das walk out to the middle to open the batting for Bangladesh. Tim Southee to bowl the first over with the new ball.
